questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The fibrous layer of the perichondrium is composed of dense connective tissue proper and contains flattened, multipotential cells resembling fibroblasts. These cells round up and differentiate into the chondroblasts located in the chondrogenic layer. The fibrous layer serves as a reserve-cell source for the chondrogenic layer and as protection for the cartilage.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The chondrogenic layer of the perichondrium is interposed between the fibrous layer and cartilage tissue proper. This layer contains chondroblasts lying adjacent to the cartilage. Chondroblasts surround themselves with cartilage matrix, thus becoming chondrocytes and increasing the thickness of the cartilage by appositional growth.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the tissue indicated by the arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Hyaline cartilage proper is composed of cells (chondrocytes) and their surrounding extracellular matrix. Chondrocytes are usually present as isogenous groups. The glassy (hyaline) extracellular matrix is composed of a firm-rubber ground substance and collagen (type II) fibrils.

questoes.enunciado: What is the specific name of the region around the tips of the arrows?

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The darkly staining extracellular matrix immediately around an isogenous group is called the territorial matrix and represents an area where glycosaminoglycans are highly concentrated.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Chondroblasts in the chondrogenic layer secrete cartilage matrix around themselves, becoming chondrocytes and increasing cartilage thickness by appositional growth. The exact point at which a chondroblast becomes a chondrocyte is hard to visualize. The transition, however, of inactive, flattened cells to plump, secretory chondroblasts to spherical chondrocytes is well shown.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the tisue that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The qualities that distinguish elastic cartilage are quite evident here: numerous chondrocytes with few isogenous groups, less extracellular matrix than hyaline cartilage and abundant, very obvious elastic fibers.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Fibrocartilage can be difficult to differentiate from dense connective tissue. Rounded chondrocytes, frequently with visible cytoplasm and lacunae, differentiate fibrocartilage from connective tissue proper. Fibroblasts are distinguished by their flattened, heterochromatic nuclei and lack of visible cytoplasm and lacunae.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the tissue indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Fibrocartilage, the strongest of the cartilages, blends the strength of dense CT with that of cartilage: obvious collagen fiber bundles (similar to dense CT) and a flexible, noncompressible ground substance (similar to cartilage). Fibrocartilage exists in isolated pockets where extra strength is needed, rather than as an independent cartilage; therefore, it has no perichondrium.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. With a special stain, elastic fibers are readily visible in the elastic cartilage matrix, helping to differentiate it from hyaline cartilage.

questoes.enunciado: What is the specific name for the region in which the "X"s are located?

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The lightly staining matrix outside the dark, basophilic halo surrounding chondrocytes is called the interterritorial matrix. Glycosaminoglycans are less concentrated farther away from chondrocytes and, consequently, this area stains more palely.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells at the tips of the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Chondrocytes, chondroblasts that have completely surrounded themselves by matrix, lie in potential spaces called lacunae. Although surrounded by a firm, rubbery matrix that seems difficult to manipulate, chondrocytes produce matrix and divide (interstitial growth), forming isogenous groups. Black spheres within these cells are lipid droplets.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the type of tissue growth occurring in the cluster of cells included in the oval.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Chondrocytes lying within the cartilages divide and lay down cartilage matrix around themselves. This growth is termed interstitial growth.
